title: One Bite Here And You STAY 🍑
premise: Everyone warns visitors never to eat a peach in my aunt's valley or every road out leads back to her gate. I have visited for twelve summers and never taken a bite, and every summer the drive there gets longer, until this year it takes two days and the road behind my car is gone.
twist: The warning is backwards: the valley's road only remembers the people who have eaten there, so by never eating I was being forgotten a little more each year. I eat one, the drive home takes twelve minutes, and my mom, who stopped eating them when she moved away, finds the turn again.
world: A green valley of peach orchards under a blue sky: a white farmhouse with a porch swing and a wooden gate, a gas station with a striped awning, a row of mailboxes, a winding two-lane ridge road.
